overall_safety_summary: The scene shows a person chopping ingredients with unsafe hand positioning near a knife, and a pot handle protruding over the edge of the stove, presenting risks of cuts and accidental bumps.

hazards.description: The user is chopping ingredients with their non-dominant hand flat and fingers extended close to the knife blade.
hazards.explanation: Extending fingers flat on the cutting board instead of using a claw grip significantly increases the risk of accidental cuts if the knife slips.
hazards.older_adult_relevance: Older adults may have reduced skin thickness, slower reflexes, or hand tremors, making them more vulnerable to severe cuts from improper knife-handling.
hazards.recommended_action: Adopt the 'claw grip' technique by curling the fingertips inward to guide the knife safely.

hazards.description: A pan handle is protruding outwards over the edge of the stove on the left side of the counter.
hazards.explanation: A handle sticking out past the counter edge can easily be bumped, potentially knocking the pan over and causing spills or burns.
hazards.older_adult_relevance: Older adults with mobility aids or reduced peripheral vision are more likely to accidentally bump into protruding handles.
hazards.recommended_action: Turn the pan handle inward so it does not project over the edge of the stove or counter.

uncertainties: Whether the stove burner under the pan is currently turned on or hot.
